description: Say which paths a `.gitignore` or `.dockerignore` ignores AND BY WHICH LINE — it is `git check-ignore -v` without git. And it does what no other tool does: it reads the SAME file as git and as Docker and points at where they do NOT decide the same. The two formats look alike and are not: a pattern with no slashes (`node_modules`) applies at any depth in git but ONLY at the root in Docker, so a `.dockerignore` copied from a `.gitignore` pulls into the build context exactly what you thought you had excluded. It also warns about the `!` that cannot work because its folder is already excluded, which is the number-one cause of "my exception does nothing".
